scope: exact two-label source/counterterm theorem and minimal one-loop spurion proxy; not a full Pati-Salam beta-function calculation

setup.coefficientColumns: k_i=(k_Di,k_Mi)^T for mediator or matching copies i
setup.commonLineLaw: k_i=Lambda_i c with one nonzero c=(c_D,c_M)^T
setup.oneLoopFlow: dot(k_i)=A_i k_i+s_i, where A_i contains label anomalous dimensions and mixing and s_i is additive counterterm support evaluated on the common-line locus

exactMinorEvolution.rankOneTangency: the common-line variety is one-loop invariant exactly when this expression vanishes for every active pair i,j
exactMinorEvolution.homogeneousCriterion: when all s_i vanish, tangency is equivalent to (A_i-A_j)c lying in span(c) for every i,j
exactMinorEvolution.universalProjectiveSufficientCondition: A_i=A+alpha_i I for one common label-mixing matrix A
exactMinorEvolution.fixedLineCriterion: the fixed ray span(c) is invariant exactly when det(c,A_i c+s_i/Lambda_i)=0 for every i with nonzero Lambda_i
exactMinorEvolution.homogeneousFixedLineCriterion: with s_i=0, c must be a common eigenvector of every A_i

ratioEvolution.matrixConvention: A=[[a,b],[q,d]], beta_D=a k_D+b k_M, beta_M=q k_D+d k_M
ratioEvolution.ratio: r=k_M/k_D on the k_D nonzero patch
ratioEvolution.interpretation: a universal A preserves alignment of all copies while generally rotating their common projective ray; a fixed c_M/c_D requires an eigenline

fixedRatio: a non-anomalous Ward identity acts on the completed invariant operator/source space
the allowed portal counterterm source module is one-dimensional and spanned by c
every multiplicative pole maps c to a scalar multiple of c
every additive pole has zero component transverse to c
threshold matching and canonical normalization preserve the same embedded line
runningCommonRay: all copies have the same projective anomalous action, differing at most by scalar rescaling on the selected line
copy-dependent additive poles have one common transverse velocity after division by Lambda_i

exchangeZ2Proxy.closure: an invariant additive pole lies in the chosen fixed ray, so the exact non-anomalous exchange Ward identity protects the corresponding fixed ratio

wardClosureConditions.physicalBoundary: O_D and O_M use inequivalent Pati-Salam scalar and family-charge dressings. Existing gauge and family Ward identities distinguish rather than exchange them, so they do not enforce gamma_D=gamma_M or a common eigenline. The formal portal-label Z2 of claim 1528 would do so only if it lifts to a non-anomalous symmetry of normalized completed operators and their regulator, thresholds, and counterterms.

counterexample.conclusion: different Majorana-label anomalous dimensions generate a transverse projective minor immediately

universalRunningRay.conclusion: one common mixing matrix preserves rank one across copies but does not preserve the fixed ratio

wardEigenline.conclusion: a common eigenline plus scalar column rescalings preserves both alignment and the fixed ratio

additivePoleCounterexample.conclusion: even universal multiplicative running is insufficient when an allowed additive counterterm points off the line

decision.conditionalRunningAlignment: yes, under universal projective anomalous flow and compatible additive poles
decision.conditionalFixedRatio: yes, when the selected source line is an exact common Ward eigenline and all transverse additive counterterms are forbidden
decision.physicalPatiSalamStatus: underdetermined until the complete anomalous-dimension, vertex-counterterm, threshold, and portal-label Ward modules are supplied

verdict: The common coefficient-line law is not generically RG invariant. Rank-one alignment survives exactly under common projective counterterm flow, while a fixed Dirac-Majorana ratio requires the stronger common-eigenline Ward condition and absence of transverse additive poles.
